agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. PS26-27473 (Part 1 of 2)(See Item )
Resolution approving an Award Letter for the Fiscal Year 2025 Assistance to Firefighters Grant (No. EMW-2025-FG-00325) in the amount of $120,909.09 from the United States Department of Homeland Security; authorizing execution by the Mayor and attestation by the City Clerk; providing an effective date. (Part 1 of 2).
agendaItems.background: The City of Tampa applied for and was awarded a Fiscal Year 2025 Assistance to Firefighters Grant (No. EMW-2025-FG-00325) in the amount of $120,909.09. The required match for this project is $12,090.91 for a total project cost of $133,000.00. Grant funds will help bring all Company Officers in the ranks of Lieutenant and Captain to Florida's State Standards and the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards for Company Officers. The City of Tampa will provide Fire Officer I training to 30 Lieutenants, Fire Officer II training to 100 Captains, and Fire Officer III training to 20 Chief Officers. The City of Tampa will contract with a training provider to offer this hands-on, instructor-led training. After completing the training course, Fire Officers will complete a certification exam. The course books will be included in the training contract.

The City of Tampa applied for and was awarded a Fiscal Year 2025 Assistance to Firefighters

National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards for Company Officers. The City of 
Tampa will provide Fire Officer I training to 30 Lieutenants, Fire Officer II training to 100 
Captains, and Fire Officer III training to 20 Chief Officers. The City of Tampa will contract with

course, Fire Officers will complete a certification exam. The course books will be included in 
the training contract.

agendaItems.rawTitle:

agendaItems.background: Whereas, it is in the public interest of the City of Tampa ("City") to receive services from the NAACP ("Agency") for the residents of the City who are desirous of such services; and whereas, the City has determined that the best interests of its citizens shall be served by entering into an agreement with the Agency for the furnishing of services and/or facilities provided by the Agency; and whereas, it is the desire of the parties to establish the terms and conditions under which the terms of this agreement shall be implemented; and whereas, the Agency has requested assistance from the City as provided for in the SMART form attached as an exhibit to this agreement in the amount of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000); and whereas, the City has reviewed this request and is approving consideration to be provided to the Agency as provided for in section D of the agreement in an amount not to exceed seventy‑five thousand dollars ($75,000); and whereas, the City shall reimburse the Agency in an amount not to exceed seventy‑five thousand dollars ($75,000) for the purpose of a greater understanding of area history through educational and public outreach programs and to encourage an interest in history through cooperation with other historical and cultural organizations; and whereas, the term of the agreement shall commence on the effective date and expire September 30, 2026, with no guaranteed renewal for subsequent terms; and whereas, the terms and conditions provided for in the agreement will control the relationship between the City and Agency; and whereas, all services provided for under the agreement must be completed prior to September 30, 2026, for the Agency to receive the agreed‑to payments as provided for in section D of the agreement; and whereas, City Council does hereby affirm that it would be beneficial to the residents of the City to enter into this Social Action & Arts Fund Services Agreement between the City and the Agency.

Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
The City of Tampa approved a Social Action & Arts Fund Services Agreement 
between the City and the NAACP, a Florida not‑for‑profit corporation. The 
agreement was established to promote a greater understanding of area 
history through educational and public outreach programs and to encourage 
interest in history by collaborating with other historical and cultural 
organizations. The funding amount did not exceed seventy‑five thousand 
dollars ($75,000). The Mayor of the City of Tampa was authorized to execute 
the agreement, and the resolution was given an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
Whereas, it is in the public interest of the City of Tampa ("City") to receive services from the 
NAACP ("Agency") for the residents of the City who are desirous of such services; and 
whereas, the City has determined that the best interests of its citizens shall be served by 
entering into an agreement with the Agency for the furnishing of services and/or facilities 
provided by the Agency; and whereas, it is the desire of the parties to establish the terms and 
conditions under which the terms of this agreement shall be implemented; and whereas, the 
Agency has requested assistance from the City as provided for in the SMART form attached 
as an exhibit to this agreement in the amount of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000); 
and whereas, the City has reviewed this request and is approving consideration to be 
provided to the Agency as provided for in section D of the agreement in an amount not to 
exceed seventy‑five thousand dollars ($75,000); and whereas, the City shall reimburse the 
Agency in an amount not to exceed seventy‑five thousand dollars ($75,000) for the purpose 
of a greater understanding of area history through educational and public outreach programs 
and to encourage an interest in history through cooperation with other historical and cultural 
organizations; and whereas, the term of the agreement shall commence on the effective date 
and expire September 30, 2026, with no guaranteed renewal for subsequent terms; and 
whereas, the terms and conditions provided for in the agreement will control the relationship 
between the City and Agency; and whereas, all services provided for under the agreement 
must be completed prior to September 30, 2026, for the Agency to receive the agreed‑to 
payments as provided for in section D of the agreement; and whereas, City Council does 
hereby affirm that it would be beneficial to the residents of the City to enter into this Social 
Action & Arts Fund Services Agreement between the City and the Agency.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes

FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This Resolution approves an agreement between the City of Tampa and NAACP for an 
amount not to exceed $75,000  to promote a greater understanding of area history through 
educational and public outreach programs; and to encourage an interest in history through 
cooperation with other historical and cultural organization. Funds are available from General 
Fund Non-Departmental Social Action and Arts funding.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. NCA26-27398
Resolution approving a Social Action & Arts Fund services agreement between the City of Tampa, Florida and Mentors for Hillsborough County Veterans - Veterans Treatment Court, a Florida not-for-profit corporation, to promote increased access for veterans' services in an amount not to exceed twenty-four thousand nine hundred ninety-nine dollars ($24,999), authorizing the execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
It is in the public interest of the City of Tampa (“City”) to receive services from the Mentors of Hillsborough County Veterans–Veterans Treatment Court (“Agency”) for residents of the City who are desirous of such services. The City has determined that the best interests of its citizens will be served by entering into an agreement with the Agency for the furnishing of services and/or facilities provided by the Agency. The parties desire to establish the terms and conditions under which this agreement will be implemented. The Agency has requested assistance from the City as provided for in the SMART Form attached as an exhibit to the agreement in the amount of thirty‑nine thousand four hundred forty‑eight dollars ($39,448).

The City has reviewed this request and is approving consideration to be provided to the Agency as outlined in section D of the agreement in an amount not to exceed twenty‑four thousand nine hundred ninety‑nine dollars ($24,999). The City will reimburse the Agency in an amount not to exceed Mentors of Hillsborough County Veterans–Veterans Treatment Court for the purpose of increased access to veteran services. The term of the agreement will commence on the effective date and expire on September 30, 2026, with no guaranteed renewal for subsequent terms. The terms and conditions outlined in the agreement will control the relationship between the City and the Agency. All services provided under the agreement must be completed prior to September 30, 2026, for the Agency to receive the payments specified in section D of the agreement. The City Council affirms that entering into this Social Action & Arts Fund Services Agreement between the City and the Agency will be beneficial to the residents of the City.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. INF26-26359
Resolution accepting the proposal of Bayside Dredging LLC pertaining to Contract 26-C-00027 Stormwater Pond Dredging and Restoration Contract FY26, in the amount of $1,650,000; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa to execute said contract on behalf of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
1. Background: a. Contract Title: 26-C-00027 Stormwater Pond Dredging and Restoration Contract FY26 b. Address of Project: Various locations throughout the City c. Number of bidders/submitters: Two (2) d.    Names of bidders/submitters: • Bayside Dredging LLC • Asphalt Millings Inc.

e. Dollar amount: $1,650,000.00

2.    Why the awardee was selected: Contractor was selected via hard bid

3. Contractor/Firm: Bayside Dredging LLC

4.    Business Case:  Project provides for improving stormwater ponds throughout the City.

Services include dredging existing stormwater ponds, removing and disposing of sediments, debris, and invasive vegetation, embankment restoration and erosion control restoration.

This is a one (1) year contract that can be renewed for three (3) additional one (1) year period at the same prices, terms and conditions, Work is issued by location on a work order basis.

5. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement:  Bayside Dredging LLC. , the prime contractor, is committed to utilizing 1 city-certified firm for subcontracting.

6. Sustainability and Resiliency: The project provides for stormwater pond improvements at various locations throughout the City. This project is consistent with Transforming Tampa's Tomorrow goal of Sustainability and Resiliency and is integral to protect properties and infrastructure from flood damage.

Community Engagement: The Mobility Public Relations and CAD Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CAD-CEI) team will assist the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Bid- Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) •  365 consecutive calendar days.

• The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.background: WHEREAS, as approved by Resolution No. 2021-221, the Florida Department of Transportation and the City of Tampa entered into a Utility Work by Highway Contractor Master Agreement on April 20, 2021 (“Master Agreement”); and WHEREAS, the Florida Department of Transportation is currently engaging in a project which involves constructing, reconstructing, or otherwise changing a public road identified as Project ID No.: 440511-8-56-01, Description: USB41/N TAMPA ST FROM FLORIBRASKA TO TYLER & FLORIDA FROM TYLER TO PALM hereinafter referred to as the “Project”; and WHEREAS, the City of Tampa owns certain water utility facilities which are located within the limits of the Project, hereinafter referred to as the “Facilities” (said term shall be deemed to include utility facilities as the same may be relocated, adjusted, or placed out of service); and WHEREAS, the Project requires modifications to the Facilities, primarily consisting of adjustment of valve and manhole cover lids, hereinafter referred to as “Utility Work” and referenced by the Florida Department of Transportation as financial project identification number 440511-8-56-01; and WHEREAS, on April 16, 2026, the City and the Florida Department of Transportation approved Resolution No. 2026-280, approving Change Order No. 1 and its related Escrow Agreement, in which the City agreed to pay Two Hundred and Ten Thousand Dollars ($210,000) towards the completion of the Utility Work; and WHEREAS, the Florida Department of Transportation notified the City that the estimated cost to complete the Utility Work has increased to Two Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Seven Hundred and Forty-Eight dollars and Thirty-Five Cents ($285,748.35), creating a deficit of Seventy-Five Thousand Seven Hundred and Forty-Eight Dollars and thirty-five cents ($75,748.35) between the amount previously paid by the City and the current cost; and WHEREAS, the City has agreed to contribute Twenty-One Thousand Dollars ($21,000.00) towards the deficit; and WHEREAS, pursuant to the Master Agreement, a Three Party Escrow Agreement must be executed in association with the Change Order No. 2; and WHEREAS, in consideration of the premises and the mutual covenants contained in the Master Agreement and the Change Order No. 2, and the cost efficiencies to the benefit of the City of Tampa because the Florida Department of Transportation is completing the Utility Work, it is in the best interest of the citizens of the City authorize the additional payment of Twenty-One Thousand Dollars ($21,000.00) to FDOT and to enter into Three Party Escrow Agreement under the terms and conditions set forth therein.

agendaItems.rawTitle:

agendaItems.background: The City of Tampa owns 1812 North Highland Avenue Tampa, Florida ("the Property"), otherwise known as Water Works Park. The Property is subject to a Brownfield Site Rehabilitation Agreement ("BSRA") entered into between the City and the Environmental Protection Commission ("EPC") on December 12, 2013. Per the BSRA, a Site Rehabilitation Completion Report ("Report") was completed. The Report indicates that there is soil contamination on the Property as defined by Chapter 62-780, Florida Administrative Code, but that monitoring has demonstrated groundwater contaminants were below Cleanup Target Levels, which is appropriate for a Brownfield Site. A Declaration of Restrictive Covenant ("DRC") establishes use restrictions meant to reduce or eliminate the risk of exposure or migration of contaminants at or from the Property. Upon this DRC being recorded in the Public Records of Hillsborough County, the EPC will issue a Site Rehabilitation Completion Order. The City of Tampa is willing to execute and abide by the DRC.

agendaItems.background:
Background: a. Contract Title: HFC AWTP SCADA Migration and Fiber Replacement Design b. Address of Project: 2700 Maritime Blvd., Tampa, FL 33605 c. Number of bidders/submitters: 3 (Three) d.Names of bidders/submitters: • Hazen and Sawyer, P.C • McKim & Creed, Inc.

• US Water Services Corporation e.Dollar amount: • The total Contract estimate will be $2,000,000-$4,000,000 • This Initial design agreement is for $475,468.65 f. Why was the awardee selected: Most qualified, according to CCNA Committee scores.

2. Contractor/Firm: McKim & Creed, Inc.

3.Business Case: • The project is to obtain Professional Engineering services for the work necessary to complete the migration of Howard F. Curren AWTP (HFC AWTP) Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system from HSQ software to VTScada software. The project also includes the design for the replacement of the treatment plant’s fiber optic cable network. The project aims to improve efficiency, monitoring, control, and security of the HFC AWTP processes by implementing a unified and updated SCADA system.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: McKim & Creed, Inc., the prime contractor, is committed to utilizing one (1) city-certified firm for subcontracting.

5.Sustainability and Resiliency: Green, Social and Sustainable Framework: This project is eligible under the framework as is provides sustainable stormwater management and pollution prevention and control.

6. Community Engagement: The Contract Administration Department’s Engineering and Inspection team will assist the Contractor in all communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a.Contract delivery method: This is a Design project.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) • 10 months.

• The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. INF26-27459
Resolution accepting the Proposal of C & T Contracting Services, LLC Pertaining to Contract 26-C-00042 Forest Hills Park Pump Station Replacement, in the amount of $1,565,000; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa To execute said contract on behalf of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
Background:

1. Contract Title: 26-C-00042 Forest Hills Park Pump Station Replacement a. Address of Project: 709 W. Bougainvillea Ave. Tampa, FL 33612.

b. Number of bidders/submitters: 3 (three) c.    Names of bidders/submitters: • C & T Contracting Services, LLC • Cathcart Construction Company – Florida, LLC • Nelson Construction Company LLC d. Dollar amount: $1,565,000.00 e.    Why the awardee was selected: The lowest qualified and responsive bidder was selected pursuant to FS 255.20.

1. Contractor/Firm: C & T Contracting Services, LLC

2.    Business Case: This project provides for the installation of an automated pump station to replace the existing temporary pump station at the Forest Hills Park along West Bougainvillea Avenue. The work includes installation of wet well, pumps, SCADA system, electrical and control equipment, emergency generator, piping, site improvements, park restoration, and all associated appurtenances required to provide a complete and operational system in accordance with the Contract Documents.

Work shall also include demolition, removal, and disposal of existing structures and equipment; coordination of City-purchased equipment with the City and equipment suppliers; receipt, unloading, storage, protection, installation, testing, startup, and integration of City-purchased items into the pump station system; site restoration; and all other work necessary to deliver a fully functional and operational facility.

3. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: C & T Contracting Services, LLC , the prime contractor, is utilizing three (3) City of Tampa-certified firms for subcontracting.

4. Sustainability and Resiliency: The new pump station will eliminate the need for maintenance personnel to operate the pump station during wet weather conditions and will provide a more reliable means to control upstream water levels. This station will be controlled remotely through the City's SCADA system.

5. Community Engagement: The Mobility Public Relations and CAD Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CAD-CEI) team will assist the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

6. Project: a.    Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Bid-Build project.

b. Placemaking: N/A c.    Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget): • 240 consecutive calendar days.

• A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality  of construction.

• The Trimble Unity Construct project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. Trimble Unity Construct is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. INF26-27470 (Part 1 of 2)(See Item )
Resolution authorizing an Amendment to the Agreement for Consultant Services between the City of Tampa and Jacobs Engineering Group Inc. regarding Contract 23-D-00015-CSA01 Facility Master Plan – Water Department; authorizing the Mayor to execute said Amendment on behalf of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
1. Contract Title: 23-D-00015 Facility Master Plan a. Address of Project: Citywide b. Number of bidders/submitters: N/A c. Names of bidders/submitters: N/A d. Dollar amount: $997,610 e. Why the awardee was selected: Firm was selected pursuant to F.S. 287.055 Consultant Competitive Negotiation Act.

2. Contractor/Firm: Jacobs Engineering Group Inc.

3. Business Case: The project provides for the development of a Facility Master Plan for a planning horizon of ten years (2024 – 2034). The master planning process will include: • An assessment of the currently owned properties and their occupancy purposes.

• Evaluation of the business needs of the Department as it relates to buildings and personnel.

• Identification of limitations of the current utilization of the properties as it relates to business functions.

• Evaluation and identification of improvements and efficiencies needed to maximize business operations.

• Identification of areas where solar energy can be implemented along with the most optimal utilization of the property.

• Development of a program of improvements to include a prioritized list of projects, conceptual plans, their probable construction cost, and schedule of implementation using risk-based prioritization.

• Recommendations regarding the method (or methods) of project delivery that will best serve the Water Department for the recommended improvements.

The Master Plan will consider real estate owned or leased for use by the Water Department, consisting of eight sites. The plan will also evaluate betterment options including acquisition or leased property.

This Amendment 1 provides for the preparation of construction documents, submittal coordination for building permits, and responses to comments as related to the Morris Bridge Pump Station and Wellfield Facility.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: JACOBS ENGINEERING GROUP INC , the prime contractor, is utilizing three (3) City of Tampa-certified firms for subcontracting.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: The resulting Master Plan document will describe the rationale and technical basis for the recommended program of improvements creating a defensible plan to guide the growth of the Water Department for the next decade.

6. Community Engagement: This master plan development does not involve public engagement.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) • 168 consecutive calendar days.

• The Trimble project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.rawTitle:

Resolution authorizing Change Order 2 to the Agreement deducting $1,886,910.73 to Contract 19-C-00059 Lower Peninsula Stormwater Improvements Project – Southeast Region – Design Build, between the City of Tampa and Kimmins Contracting Corp.; authorizing execution of Change Order 2 by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
1. Background: a. Contract Title: Lower Peninsula Stormwater Improvements Project – Southeast Region Design-Build b. Dollar amount: ($1,886,910.73) c. Why the awardee was selected: Selected Pursuant to FS 287.055 CCNA

2. Contractor/Firm:  Kimmins Contracting Corporation

3. Business Case: This Agreement provided for a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for the Lower Peninsula Stormwater Improvements Project – Southeast Region Project. The project included the construction of approximately 10,000 linear feet of box culvert, pipes, laterals, inlets, interconnections through a regional pond, a proposed outfall to Old Tampa Bay, passive park amenities and associated utility construction and/ or relocation.

The initial Agreement provided for professional engineering services for design, permitting, scheduling cost estimating, engineering and inspection (CEI), administering subcontracts, and all related work required for a completed project.

Change Order 1 provided for escalation of boardwalk upgrades, fencing, picnic shelter, benches, trach receptacles, bike rack and sidewalk accessories. Work also included upsizing a watermain from a 2 inch to a 6 inch and an additional fire hydrant.

Change Order 2, Final provides for establishment of Substantial Completion Date, adjustment of the Final Contract Amount (a reduction), as well as Final Payment to the Contractor.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement:  Kimmins Contracting Corp. , the prime contractor, has utilized twelve (12) City of Tampa-certified firms for subcontracting.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: Project provided for stormwater improvements within the Lower Peninsula basin. This project is consistent with Transforming Tampa's Tomorrow goal of Sustainability and Resiliency.

6. Community Engagement: The Mobility Public Relations and CAD Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CAD-CEI) team will assist the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector was on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) •  0 consecutive calendar days.

•  The e-Builder project management software system was utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. F26-26158
Resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida, establishing an Auditor Selection Committee; in accordance with Section 218.391, Florida Statutes; providing for committee purpose, membership, and duties.
agendaItems.background:
The City's current auditor, Forvis Mazars, LLP, will end with the completion of the FY26 Audit in March 2027. The new audit firm will need to be under contract prior to June 2027 to allow for pre-testing activities in preparation for auditing the City's FY2027 financials.

Florida Statutes requires the establishment of an Auditor Selection Committee comprised of at least three members; however, the Chief Financial Officer recommends having four members to ensure continuity of effort throughout the review process. The Chair of the Auditor Selection Committee must be a member of the City Council and will serve as the committee's chairperson. Resolution making certain changes in the budget of the City of Tampa for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; approving the transfer, reallocation, and/or appropriation of $332,629 within the Downtown/Ybor Tourism Marketing District Fund to provide tourism marketing services within the district; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. F26-27476
Resolution making certain changes in the budget of the City of Tampa for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; approving the transfer, reallocation, and/or appropriation of $332,629 within the Downtown/Ybor Tourism Marketing District Fund to provide tourism marketing services within the district; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
Ordinance No. 2017-42, amended by Ordinance 2020-54, created the Downtown/Historic Ybor Tourism Marketing District (TMD) and established a process for levying and collecting a tourism marketing non-ad valorem special assessment.

Resolution 2021-106 was approved by City Council on February 4, 2021 to delegate the power and authority to manage and administer the affairs of the District to the Hillsborough County Hotel and Motel Association, Inc., for a twenty-year term.

The non-ad valorem special assessment provides for tourism marketing services within the TMD aiming to attract overnight visitors and reach additional market segments needed to ensure the City and the District remain a competitive tourism market.

The non-ad valorem special assessment is paid by specific tourism properties located within the TMD that are receiving a benefit from this assessment and are included in the tourism marketing non-ad valorem assessment roll. The assessment is based on a fixed rate charged to the total number of hotel rooms. The assessment is collected by the Hillsborough County Tax Collector’s Office and submitted to the City, net of administrative costs (1%). The City of Tampa submits the revenue received from the Tax Collector’s Office to the Hillsborough County Hotel and Motel Association on a monthly basis, net of administrative costs (1%).

FY2026 Voluntary Contributions: This Resolution appropriates additional FY2026 revenue in the amount of $332,629 collected by the Hillsborough Tax Collector’s Office and provided by certain participating hotels included within the non-ad valorem assessment roll for an amount that exceeded their FY2026 assessment.  Based on the information provided by the Hotel & Motel Association, the Downtown/Historic Ybor Tourism Marketing District (TMD) approved the commitment to installment payments in connection with the recruitment of convention groups in FY2024 – FY2026, called the TMD Convention Concession Fund.  As a result, many of the participating hotels have decided to pay more than their assessment, with the understanding that the surplus will allow the TMD to maintain its digital marketing campaign commitment, which allows for generating supplemental room revenue with leisure-based business while growing its convention group recruitment and retention program.

Pursuant to Section 166.241(8)(a), under certain circumstances a local government within 60 days following the end of the fiscal year may amend a budget for that year.

BACKGROUND:
Metropolitan Charities, Inc. was awarded a 3-year HOPWA Agreement to provide Short-Term 
Rent, Mortgage, and Utilities assistance and Supportive Services for persons with HIV/AIDS 
and their affected resident family members in order to create housing stability and reduce the 
risk of homelessness in Hillsborough County.

the provision of services in support of Persons with Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome 
(AIDS) under the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development HOPWA program in 
an amount of $297,000 per year for 3 years. Subrecipient shall be reimbursed for Short Term 
Rent, Mortgage and Utilities, and Supportive Services assistance in an amount not to exceed 
$297,000 per year for 3 years from the Housing and Community Development Department’s 
HOPWA Grant Funds.  During the first year of the three-year funding cycle, reimbursement 
shall not exceed $297,000.00 in Grant Funds for Fiscal Year 2027. Subsequent 
reimbursement payments shall not annually exceed $297,000.00 in funds for Fiscal Year 
2028 and Fiscal Year 2029 and are contingent upon available funds approved and provided 
by the U.S. Department of HUD and City Council approval.

Resolution approving the execution by the Mayor and attestation by the City Clerk of a Lease Agreement between the City of Tampa and Dream Center of Tampa, Inc., a Florida not for profit corporation, leasing City-owned property located at 2806 N. 15th Street for recreational, educational, and accessory daycare programs that are limited to underserved residents and intended for individual and community growth and development; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. DEO26-27434
Resolution approving the execution by the Mayor and attestation by the City Clerk of a Lease Agreement between the City of Tampa and Dream Center of Tampa, Inc., a Florida not for profit corporation, leasing City-owned property located at 2806 N. 15th Street for recreational, educational, and accessory daycare programs that are limited to underserved residents and intended for individual and community growth and development; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The City of Tampa owns real property located at 2806 N. 15th Street, Tampa, Florida, improved with a 19,050 square foot building.

The City and Dream Center entered into a Commercial Lease Agreement, dated December 15, 2015 and approved by Resolution 2015-1028, as amended by that First Amendment to Commercial Lease Agreement, dated March 10, 2017 and approved by Resolution 2017-205, to provide recreational and daycare programs to the general public. This Lease expired on December 14, 2025, and Dream Center is currently holding over occupancy.

The City advertised a Request for Proposal soliciting proposals from qualified 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations to lease the property for recreational, educational, and accessory daycare programs that are limited to underserved residents and intended for individual and community growth and development. The Dream Center’s proposal was accepted. The City and Dream Center desire to enter into a new Lease Agreement under the terms and conditions stated therein.

agendaItems.background:
1. Background: a. Contract Title: Drew Park Lois Avenue and Grady Avenue Landscape and Streetscape; b. Dollar amount:  $250,000.00 c. Why the awardee was selected: Competitive bid

2.    Contractor/Firm: Cathcart Construction Company - Florida, LLC

3. Business Case: Project provides for replacing and maintaining  trees and landscaping, relocate existing landscaping where necessary to optimize space and functionality, upgrade the irrigation systems to ensure efficient water use and support new plantings, and modify plant species to enhance ecological benefits and aesthetic appeal.  Project work is limited within the Drew Park CRA District within the right of way along Lois and Grady Avenues (W Crest Ave to W Dr. Martin Luther King Jr Blvd).

Change Order 1 provides for cost increase, additional pay items and extends contract time

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement:  To date, CATHCART CONSTRUCTION COMPANY - FLORIDA, LLC, has utilized 2 city-certified firms for subcontracting participation

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: The project provides for improvements within the  Drew Park CRA District within the right of way along Lois and Grady Avenues (W Crest Ave to W Dr.

Martin Luther King Jr Blvd). This project is consistent with Transforming Tampa's Tomorrow goal of Sustainability and Resiliency..

6. Community Engagement: The CRA and CAD Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CAD-CEI) team will assist the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Bid-Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) •  90 consecutive calendar days.

• The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.background:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection administers the Brownfield Remediation Program under Ch. 376, F.S. Upon designation, a Person Responsible for Site Rehabilitation enters into a Brownfield Site Rehabilitation Agreement with the State or delegated local government. Assignment and Assumptions of the BSRA require consent from the local government with jurisdiction over the real property where the brownfield site is located.

The City of Tampa has been requested, as the local government with jurisdiction over the real property where the brownfield site is located, to authorize the assignment and assumption of the BSRA between Urban Tampa Db Hotel Owner, LLC and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection to the proposed assignee, PR FH Tampa Property, LLC.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. DEO26-27667
Resolution submitting the City of Tampa Community Development Block Grant - Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) project list for consideration and approval by the City Council of the City of Tampa.
Memorandum from Michael Perry, Deputy Chief Financial Officer, transmitting additional information for said agenda item. (To be R/F)
agendaItems.background:
CDBG‑DR is a supplemental federal funding program administered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to assist communities recovering from presidentially declared disasters. These funds are designed to support long‑term recovery by addressing unmet needs that remain after other federal assistance programs have been exhausted.

In 2024, the State of Florida experienced significant impacts from Hurricanes Helene and Milton, both of which resulted in widespread damage to housing, infrastructure, and critical community facilities. Following these events and the resulting disaster declarations, HUD allocated CDBG‑DR funding to support recovery efforts throughout affected regions.

Hillsborough County was designated as the Primary Grantee for these CDBG‑DR funds and is responsible for administering the program locally in accordance with federal requirements.

As part of this role, Hillsborough County has notified the City of Tampa that the City is eligible to submit project proposals for consideration to receive subrecipient allocations under the County’s CDBG‑DR award.

The County will evaluate all proposed projects to determine their eligibility and alignment with CDBG‑DR program objectives, including meeting documented recovery needs, benefiting impacted populations, and complying with HUD regulations.

Projects that are selected for funding will undergo an additional review and approval process, which will include formal action through a future resolution and a subrecipient agreement that outlines roles, responsibilities, and compliance requirements.

Given the severity of impacts experienced during the 2024 hurricane season, it is in the best interest of the City of Tampa and its residents to proactively address critical infrastructure vulnerabilities. Advancing projects that strengthen resilience and support long‑term community recovery is essential for protecting residents, supporting equitable redevelopment, and reducing the risk of future disaster‑related harm.

File No. PH26-27129
Resolution setting a public hearing before the City Council of the City of Tampa on November 19, 2026 at 1:30 p.m., or soon thereafter, in City Council Chambers, 315 E. Kennedy Blvd., 3rd Floor, Tampa, FL 33602, to consider whether to opt-out of the property tax exemption for certain multifamily projects that provide affordable housing in the 80% - 120% range of the median annual adjusted gross income, which properties would otherwise be eligible for an exemption from ad valorem taxation pursuant to Section 196.1978(3)(d)1.a., Florida Statutes; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. PH26-27129
Resolution setting a public hearing before the City Council of the City of Tampa on November 19, 2026 at 1:30 p.m., or soon thereafter, in City Council Chambers, 315 E. Kennedy Blvd., 3rd Floor, Tampa, FL 33602, to consider whether to opt-out of the property tax exemption for certain multifamily projects that provide affordable housing in the 80% - 120% range of the median annual adjusted gross income, which properties would otherwise be eligible for an exemption from ad valorem taxation pursuant to Section 196.1978(3)(d)1.a., Florida Statutes; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
Section 196.1978(3), Florida Statutes, requires the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser to exempt certain qualifying rental properties from ad valorem taxation when such properties meet the statutory criteria for multifamily projects that provide affordable housing to households within specified income limits. Section 196.1978(3)(d)1.a. of the Florida Statutes provides a 75% ad valorem tax exemption es (i.e. 75% of the assessed property value is exempt from property taxes)  for affordable housing that serves persons or families whose annual household income is greater than 80 percent but not more than 120 percent of the median annual adjusted gross income ("AMI")  for households within that metropolitan statistical area("MSA").

However, in its 2024 session, the Florida Legislature adopted a bill (HB 7073, Laws of Florida Ch. 2024-158)  that allows taxing authorities such as the City of Tampa to annually "opt-out" of providing that exemption if the three previous years Shimberg Center for Housing Studies Annual Reports which are prepared at the University of Florida per Sec. 420.6075, Florida Statutes ("Shimberg Annual Reports") determine that the number of available afforable units is an MSA is greater than the number of renter households in the MSA for the category entitled 0-120% AMI.  It is necessary to hold a public hearing on the proposed resolution to receive public comment and allow the Tampa City Council to consider whether to approve the proposed opt-out of the 80–120 Tax Exemption.

Resolution approving a Subrecipient Agreement between the Office of the State Attorney for the 13th Judicial Circuit in and for Hillsborough County ("SAO") and City of Tampa ("City") on behalf of the Tampa Police Department ("TPD") for purposes of purchasing Peregrine; authorizing the execution thereof  the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date. (Continued from September 17, 2026)(Motion to reschedule initiated by Hurtak-Miranda on October 1, 2026 from November 5, 2026 to October 15, 2026)
agendaItems.background: The SAO will pay the City $595,000 from specific appropriation 897 of Chapter 2024-23, continued under 2025 and 2026 General Appropriations Act, for the purpose of purchasing Peregrine, a CJIS-aligned SaaS platform for public safety which will unify various operational systems into a single platform improving efficiency, safety, response and investigations for TPD and aid in Ybor crime reduction (hereinafter "the Grant").  The funding described above and the purchase by City for TPD of this technology will be for the use of Peregrine in order to enhance public safety, provide real-time information to law enforcement, assist with crime scene investigations, and document evidence.  The funding is to provide dedicated use of Peregrine technology by TPD as part of its overall public safety plan for Ybor City and the City of Tampa.  As a condition of receiving these grant funds, City shall comply with all applicable Florida Statutes.  Accepting this Grant will provide a public safety benefit to the citizens of Tampa.

SubjectA resolution approving a Subrecipient Agreement between the SAO of

Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
A resolution approving a Subrecipient Agreement between the Office of the 
State Attorney for the 13th Judicial Circuit in and for Hillsborough County 
("SAO") and City of Tampa ("City") on behalf of the Tampa Police Department 
("TPD") for purposes of purchasing Peregrine; authorizing the execution 
thereof  the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.  Part 1 of 
2.
BACKGROUND:
The SAO will pay the City $595,000 from specific appropriation 897 of Chapter 2024-23, 
continued under 2025 and 2026 General Appropriations Act, for the purpose of purchasing 
Peregrine, a CJIS-aligned SaaS platform for public safety which will unify various operational 
systems into a single platform improving efficiency, safety, response and investigations for 
TPD and aid in Ybor crime reduction (hereinafter "the Grant").  The funding described above 
and the purchase by City for TPD of this technology will be for the use of Peregrine in order to 
enhance public safety, provide real-time information to law enforcement, assist with crime 
scene investigations, and document evidence.  The funding is to provide dedicated use of 
Peregrine technology by TPD as part of its overall public safety plan for Ybor City and the City 
of Tampa.  As a condition of receiving these grant funds, City shall comply with all applicable 
Florida Statutes.  Accepting this Grant will provide a public safety benefit to the citizens of 
Tampa.

FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This resolution approves an agreement between the Office of State Attorney and the City of 
Tampa on behalf of the Tampa Police department to receive $595,000 for purposes of the 
purchase of a CJIS-aligned SaaS platform for public safety.

agendaItems.background:
On August 27, 2026, Tampa City Council approved a development and funding agreement between the City, Hillsborough County, and Tampa Bay Rays Stadium Company, LLC (the "Agreement").  The Agreement has been executed by all parties.  Pursuant to the Agreement, the City is required to contribute $80.0 million payable in four (4) annual payments from legally available non-available revenues on a reimbursable basis (the "City Contribution Amount").

As a condition to providing the City Contribution Amount, the City is required to obtain court validation of the City Contribution Amount.  Such validation is intended to confirm the legality and authority of the City Contribution Amount and the purpose for which it is being made.

It may be necessary and/or desirable to fund all or a portion of any or all of the four (4) annual payments with debt (the "Potential Debt").  City staff and the City's public finance professionals recommend that the Potential Debt also be validated at the time the City seeks circuit court validation of the City Contribution Amount under the Agreement.  The legal issues are the same.  A successful validation of the City Contribution Amount and the Potential Debt would provide legal protection for the City.

The resolution being presented for consideration is required to be adopted in order to initiate the Circuit Court validation of the Potential Debt pursuant to Chapter 75, Florida Statutes.

The resolution authorizes the issuance of up to $80 million of indebtedness, secured by a covenant of the City to budget and appropriate sufficient legally available non-ad valorem revenues, for the purpose of funding all or a portion of the City Contribution Amount.    This resolution does not obligate the City to issue any debt for any portion of the City Contribution Amount.  It simply is required to be adopted to initiate the Circuit Court validation proceeding.

Subsequent City Council approval would be required to issue any debt for any portion of the City Contribution Amount

Tampa, Florida Non-Ad Valorem Revenue Bonds (Ballpark Project) in one or 
more series in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding $80,000,000, to 
finance and reimburse the City's contractual payment obligations under the

pay debt service on the bonds; providing for the rights of the holders of the

bonds; and providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
On August 27, 2026, Tampa City Council approved a development and funding agreement 
between the City, Hillsborough County, and Tampa Bay Rays Stadium Company, LLC (the 
"Agreement").  The Agreement has been executed by all parties.  Pursuant to the Agreement, 
the City is required to contribute $80.0 million payable in four (4) annual payments from 
legally available non-available revenues on a reimbursable basis (the "City Contribution 
Amount").  
As a condition to providing the City Contribution Amount, the City is required to obtain court 
validation of the City Contribution Amount.  Such validation is intended to confirm the legality 
and authority of the City Contribution Amount and the purpose for which it is being made.  
It may be necessary and/or desirable to fund all or a portion of any or all of the four (4) annual 
payments with debt (the "Potential Debt").  City staff and the City's public finance 
professionals recommend that the Potential Debt also be validated at the time the City seeks 
circuit court validation of the City Contribution Amount under the Agreement.  The legal 
issues are the same.  A successful validation of the City Contribution Amount and the 
Potential Debt would provide legal protection for the City.
The resolution being presented for consideration is required to be adopted in order to initiate 
the Circuit Court validation of the Potential Debt pursuant to Chapter 75, Florida Statutes.  
The resolution authorizes the issuance of up to $80 million of indebtedness, secured by a 
covenant of the City to budget and appropriate sufficient legally available non-ad valorem 
revenues, for the purpose of funding all or a portion of the City Contribution Amount.    This 
resolution does not obligate the City to issue any debt for any portion of the City Contribution 
Amount.  It simply is required to be adopted to initiate the Circuit Court validation proceeding.  

Subsequent City Council approval would be required to issue any debt for any portion of the 
City Contribution Amount
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
The resolution presented for City Council’s consideration is required to initiate Circuit Court 
validation of the potential tax exempt debt. The potential debt would fund the City’s 
contribution under the Agreement of an amount not to exceed $80,000,000 through four 
annual installments of $20,000,000.  The potential debt would be secured by a covenant to 
budget and appropriate certain legally available Non Ad Valorem Revenues.  
Adopting this resolution does not obligate the City to issue the debt, it simply initiates the 
validation process.  Any debt issuance would require subsequent City Council approval.
PROJECTED COSTS: The adoption of this Resolution is required to initiate Circuit Court 
validation of potential tax‑exempt debt for the financing of all or a portion of the City’s $80 
million Contribution Amount. The debt, if issued, would be repaid using legally available 
Non‑Ad Valorem Revenues, and any issuance would require future approval by City Council.

SubjectA Resolution authorizing an Agreement for Consultant Services in the amount 
of $3,000,000 between the City of Tampa and Alan Plummer and Associates, 
Inc. in connection with Contract 26-D-07002 Construction Engineering and 
Inspection Services.
Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
A Resolution authorizing an Agreement for Consultant Services in the amount 
of $3,000,000 between the City of Tampa and Alan Plummer and Associates, 
Inc. in connection with Contract 26-D-07002 Construction Engineering and 
Inspection Services; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa to execute 
same; providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
1.Contract Title: Construction Engineering and Inspection Services 
a. Address of Project: City wide
b. Number of bidders/submitters: 7 (Seven)
c.Names of bidders/submitters: 
•Engineered Concepts, Inc. 
• Grissom Smith, LLC
• Johnson, Mirmiran, & Thompson, Inc. (JMT)
• Alan Plummer and Associates, Inc.
• T. Y. Lin International
• V&A Consulting Engineers, Inc
• Wade Trim, Inc.
d.Dollar amount: 
• The total Contract estimate will be $3,000,000
• This Initial design agreement is for $3,000,000
• Funds will be managed through a series of subsequently issued task orders
e. Why was the awardee selected: Most qualified, according to CCNA Committee scores.
2. Contractor/Firm: Alan Plummer and Associates, Inc.
3.Business Case:  
• The project is to obtain Professional Engineering Construction Engineering and Inspection 
(CEI) services to supplement City staff in the administration, management, coordination, 
observation, inspection, documentation, startup and commissioning, and closeout of 
construction projects associated with the City's Capital Improvement Program (CIP), 
rehabilitation, maintenance, emergency response, and operational improvement initiatives.
4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: Alan Plummer and Associates, Inc , the 
prime contractor, is committed to utilizing two (2) city-certified firms for subcontracting.

5.Sustainability and Resiliency: 
Green, Social and Sustainable Framework: This project is eligible under the framework as is 
provides sustainable stormwater management and pollution prevention and control.
6. Community Engagement: The Contract Administration Department’s Engineering and 
Inspection team will assist the Contractor in all communication efforts to ensure transparency 
and integration of the stakeholders.
7. Project:
a.Contract delivery method: This is a CEI project. 
b. Placemaking: N/A
c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget)
• The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the 
monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of 
Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This Resolution provides funding in the amount of $3,000,000 for use by the Water 
Department and Wastewater Department for the D.L. Tippin Engineering and Inspections 
Services Project and the Construction Engineering and Inspection Services Project from 
within the Water Renewal and Replacement Fund, Water Future Debt Capital Projects 2028-
2031 Fund and the Wastewater Capital/Construction Fund.

4. Award amount: $7M

5. Why the winning bid was selected: The City of Tampa Parks and Recreation Department recommends awarding this to multiple Awardees for Installation, Repair, and Replacement of Parks Site Furnishings, Playground Equipment and Surfacing.

It is recommended that the City award Installation, Repair, and Replacement of Parks Site Furnishings, Playground Equipment and Surfacing to multiple Awardees for use by the Parks and Recreation Department. The term of the award is for an initial two (2) years with three (3) additional (1) one-year renewal options. The Department has reviewed and approved the bid response from multiple Awardees and comments were supplied via Department recommendation letter.

Equal Business Opportunity Statement: Phinazee Construction & Consulting Services, Inc., one (1) of the sixteen (16) contractors, is a city-certified Small Local Business Enterprise (SLBE).
